summary: Implementation-only preflight of notes/sim10_trace_20261110 (campaign.py, trace_runner.py, trace_rank.py, run.sbatch, scope.md) against accepted cc98b8440. No blockers found. trace_runner executes the accepted runner via runpy.run_path before any CuPy import, so the accepted rank/UUID mask and affinity setup happen first; helper ranks 0/1 take no GPU or timer path. Class-level patches (InputGroupPool.poll/plan_slots/issue, StagingTask.__call__, GpuEventManager._attach_gpu, bulk_accounting.accounting) are installed before main, so instances created inside main inherit them, and runner's deferred 'from bulk_accounting import accounting' picks up the wrapper. The wrapper enters after the owner-scoped cold gate and both barriers, starts cudaProfilerApi only when SIM10_NSYS_CAPTURE=1, wraps the accepted accounting with a bd.loop phase, adds no CUDA waits, and writes phases JSON after main's cleanup/barriers. Poll counters are O(1) (len of _groups, len of reclaimed tuple) and gated on recorder.active; Recorder.phase is a no-op when inactive. All instrumented methods run on the BD main thread (no threads in psana/gpu runtime). The 50000 read invariant in timing cases holds: each PendingBatch is waited exactly once (completed flag), futures are one per range, 5 ranges per event. campaign.validate preserves exact event/byte/read/callback/stream/cold-gate/cleanup/retirement checks; input metadata dict keys match native/input-stat-after.json; srun/numactl structure, controls and sbatch match accepted except 20 min limit. trace_rank profiles SLURM_PROCID 2 only, refuses to overwrite captures, uses --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi/--capture-range-end=stop with cuda,nvtx,osrt. Pure CPU timer tests (10 passed) and AST/bash -n evidence supplied by coordinator; no GPU results expected at this stage.

limitations: Read-only review; no commands executed and no tests run. Validation evidence (AST, bash -n, diff --check, 10 CPU timer tests passed) is as supplied by the coordinator.

Frozen runtime install-B at /pscratch/.../install-B is outside the worktree and could not be read (restricted mode). Compatibility of bulk_phase_timing.install() targets (e.g., GpuFileEpochs, _issue_group_reads, InputGroupPool) with install-B rather than repo HEAD is therefore unverified from this host.

findings.evidence: NSYS path is hard-coded and only resolved at os.execv on rank 2 during case 05/06. If the binary is absent, FileNotFoundError aborts after four GPU cases have already consumed premium allocation; campaign.py has no preflight for the nsys binary.
findings.requested_change: Add a cheap preflight in campaign.main before the first case (e.g., require(Path(NSYS).is_file()) or a shared constant) so a missing profiler fails before any GPU case runs. Optional: record nsys --version in provenance.json.

findings.evidence: install('Integrated-on') wraps ~35 attributes of the frozen install-B runtime by name (GpuFileEpochs, _issue_group_reads, _submit_group_gpu, InputGroupPool, etc.). Repo HEAD has them, but install-B (Oct 2026) is unreadable from this worktree, and no supplied evidence shows install() has run against install-B. A mismatch would fail only in case 02 after both clean cases.
findings.requested_change: Before the GPU job, run an import-only dry install against the frozen env (install('Integrated-on') on a node with the env active, no DataSource) or cite prior evidence that bulk_phase_timing has been installed on install-B. Fail-closed behavior is otherwise acceptable.

findings.evidence: Per-case subprocess timeout is 600 s for six cases (60 min worst case) while run.sbatch sets --time=00:20:00. No SIGTERM handler or cleanup record is written on job-limit kill, unlike the accepted campaign.
findings.requested_change: Either tighten the per-case timeout to fit the 20 min budget or add a SIGTERM handler that writes a partial/failed status file so an interrupted attempt is distinguishable from a crash. Non-blocking; job limit still bounds resource use.

findings.evidence: phases['counters']['reader'] is created lazily by observed_wait; if no wait happened while active, this raises KeyError rather than the intended require message. In the expected path 50000 is reached (one wait per PendingBatch, one future per range).
findings.requested_change: Optional: use phases['counters'].get('reader', {}) so a missing counter surfaces as a clear require failure.
